verdict.rationale: The docs show a server-side flow: you create a relay through the API, which returns a relay ID and default publish/subscribe and subscribe-only tokens. You can mint more scoped tokens with expiration times, and clients pass the token in the URL path when opening a MoQ session. No official client SDK or short end-to-end connect walkthrough is evidenced, so the client half of the story is unproven. Missing for 10: an official client SDK for connecting, a documented short end-to-end quickstart, independent hands-on corroboration of the token-to-connect flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create a session from my server, mint a scoped join token, and connect a client with the official SDK in a short documented flow

citations.quote: Cloudflare MoQ relays are available through the [Cloudflare dashboard ↗︎](https://dash.cloudflare.com/) and the [API](/api/resources/moq).
You control who can publish and who can subscribe by issuing tokens scoped to the operations each client needs.
Cloudflare returns a relay ID and two default tokens: one that can publish and subscribe, and one that can only subscribe.
You can create additional tokens and set expiration times using the [API](/api/resources/moq).
Clients send a token in the URL path when opening a MoQ session.
